serviceConfigurationFinding.finding: The Sigstore signing_config inspected on 2026-10-22 still advertised a Rekor v1 endpoint. A client version does not imply a v2 service, and installing a recent client does not activate a v2 log.
serviceConfigurationFinding.whatItMeansForB1: B1 may not assume a v2 endpoint exists. It must deploy and pin its own POSIX-backed Rekor v2 instance (§B.21), read the service metadata it actually uses (§B.10), and refuse a v1 fallback. A local slice cannot inherit a v2 endpoint from the client.

sources.note: the modules are the support that is actually present; the addendum is the register of what is pinned; the two are separate statements and neither implies a service

tensions.consequence: post-quantum checkpoint cosignatures stay on the research track (§B.26); no production cosignature claim may cite the C2SP recommendation as an available mechanism, and B1 uses the classical signature path only.
tensions.tension: ML-DSA-44 is recommended by C2SP for new deployments and is labelled experimental by the implementation.

tensions.consequence: B1 cannot inherit a v2 endpoint and B4 must read authenticated SigningConfig and TrustedRoot metadata (§B.10); any record that infers a v2 service from a client version is refused.
tensions.tension: Service configuration is not implied by client version: the inspected signing_config advertised a v1 endpoint.

tensions.consequence: B1 must derive the hashedrekord digest from the exact DSSE envelope as the admitted client does (§B.5); the envelope JSON, the payload alone and an unrelated manifest hash are not substitutes, and A10's PAE is framing, not the log-entry digest.
tensions.tension: Older documentation describes a dedicated DSSE entry type; since v2.3.0 one representation is supported and DSSE is published as hashedrekord.
